name: CyDecompilator
description: AI assisted multi-engine decompiler: native code (Ghidra, own x86/x64 C decompiler, built-in disassembler), .NET (ILSpy), Java (Vineflower), Android (JADX), Python bytecode and shaders (own DXBC/SPIR-V/DXIL engine), with an assistant that explains, renames and converts pseudo-code into real code.
author: Cyberalien

operations.name: Open file
operations.description: Open a binary, assembly, archive, bytecode or shader file as a project (deduplicated by SHA256), detect its format and, by default, analyze it with the best installed engine.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to open.

engine.description: Engine id. Empty selects the analysed (or best available) engine for the file.

force.description: Re-analyze even if an analysis already exists.

maxDecompile.description: Ghidra: functions decompiled during analysis; others on demand.

functionTimeout.description: Ghidra: decompiler timeout per function, seconds.

processor.description: Ghidra: language id for raw binaries, e.g. ARM:LE:32:v8 or x86:LE:64:default.

symbols.description: PE files: load PDB debug symbols (local folders, then the configured symbol server) and apply their names (native engine and Ghidra).

projectId.description: Project id.

operations.name: Recompilable C module
operations.description: x86 / x86-64 / ARM64: decompile functions (and, by default, everything they call) with the built-in C decompiler into ONE C file meant to compile again (MSVC / clang): globals are initialised from the image, constants inlined, prototypes emitted. Empty functions = every exported function.

projectId.description: Project id returned by open_file or list_projects.

functions.description: Functions (id, name or address). Empty = exported functions.

includeCallees.description: Also decompile every function they call.

destination.description: Absolute .c file to write. Empty = only returned.
